prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals and commitments (non-ideological)

- Tax, pensions and welfare
  - Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish the main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament. No rises in income tax or VAT.
  - “Triple Lock Plus”: uprate State Pension and a new age-related personal allowance by the highest of inflation, earnings or 2.5%.
  - Raise at least £6bn a year by tackling tax non‑compliance.
  - Maintain National Living Wage at two‑thirds of median earnings.
  - Welfare reform: tighten Work Capability Assessment (from Sep 2025); overhaul fit notes to specialist assessors; reform PIP to better target need; tougher sanctions after 12 months’ unemployment; complete transition to Universal Credit; new DWP Fraud Bill.

- Families, childcare and education
  - 30 hours free childcare for eligible parents from 9 months to school (fully in place Sept 2025); family hubs in every English local authority.
  - Child Benefit to be based on household income, tapering from £120k to £160k.
  - Mandatory National Service at 18 (paid competitive military year or civic service 25 days).
  - 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by restricting poor‑outcome degrees.
  - Ban mobile phones during the school day; introduce Advanced British Standard for 16–19; expand SEN places; expand academy trusts; lift faith school cap; teacher recruitment/retention bonuses.

- Economy, business, infrastructure and trade
  - Meet fiscal rules (debt falling, deficit <3% GDP in year 5).
  - Keep corporation tax; maintain/extend “full expensing” (including to leasing when affordable); 10‑point SME plan (rates relief, VAT threshold review, prompt payment, finance access).
  - Gigabit nationwide by 2030; standalone 5G in all populated areas.
  - Redirect £36bn from HS2 phase 2 to regional roads/rail/buses; speed up planning and cut consenting times for major schemes.
  - Public R&D to £22bn/year; large compute clusters; advanced manufacturing plan.
  - Pursue FTAs (India, GCC), implement CPTPP; maintain/defend EU TCA; ongoing regulatory reform using post‑Brexit freedoms.
  - Reduce civil service to pre‑pandemic size; productivity plans across departments; limit consultants; implement Minimum Service Levels.

- Defence, security and foreign policy
  - Defence spend to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; ≥£10bn munitions; defence R&D ≥5% of budget plus 2% for exploitation; procurement reform.
  - Ongoing support to Ukraine; National Defence and Resilience Plan.
  - Veterans Bill; veterans benefits protected and improved.

- Immigration and borders
  - Legal, binding annual cap on work/family visas, falling each year; higher salary thresholds; pre‑travel health checks; higher visa fees/IHS.
  - Implement Illegal Migration Act; monthly removals to Rwanda; returns deals; seek international asylum rule changes.
  - Parliament to set annual places on safe/legal routes.

- NHS and social care
  - NHS funding to rise above inflation annually; recruit +92,000 nurses and +28,000 doctors; expand Pharmacy First; 250 new/modernised GP surgeries; 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres.
  - Dental recovery plan; require new dentists to serve in NHS for a period.
  - £3.4bn for NHS tech (NHS App front door, AI diagnostics, data platform); cut 5,500 managers; Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco & Vapes Bill; obesity advertising limits; women’s and mental health expansions; implement Cass Review; protect single‑sex care and accommodation.

- Housing and planning
  - 1.6m homes next Parliament; fast‑track brownfield; higher inner‑London densities; reform nutrient neutrality to unlock 100k homes; development corporations.
  - New Help to Buy; permanent FTB Stamp Duty relief to £425k; Affordable Homes Programme renewal; protect Green Belt.
  - Renters Reform (abolish Section 21 with court changes); leasehold reform (cap ground rents, end forfeiture); 2‑year CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants.

- Policing, justice and protests
  - +8,000 neighbourhood police; hotspot policing nationwide; tougher sentencing (domestic murders, serious sexual/violent, knife crime); four new prisons to complete 20,000 places by 2030; fraud measures; Martyn’s Law; additional protest controls.

- Transport and drivers
  - Backing Drivers Bill: ban road pricing by any tier; reverse London ULEZ expansion; require referendums for new LTNs/20mph zones; £2 bus fare cap for entire Parliament.
  - Rail Reform Bill to create Great British Railways; national pay‑as‑you‑go contactless.

- Energy, net zero and environment
  - Annual North Sea licensing; windfall tax kept to 2028–29 (with investment allowances); new gas plants; treble offshore wind; deliver CCS clusters; approve two SMR fleets within 100 days; Wylfa gigawatt plant; grid reforms.
  - Maintain energy price cap; review standing charges; PumpWatch; energy‑efficiency vouchers; no new green levies/road pricing/frequent flyer levy; retain fracking moratorium; support rooftop/brownfield solar; protect best farmland.
  - Farming: +£1bn UK budget over Parliament; legal food security target; 50% public food spend local/higher‑standard; fast‑track farm infrastructure; five‑year tapered seasonal worker scheme.
  - Fisheries: replicate £100m Seafood Fund; seek improved inshore opportunities.
  - Water: tougher enforcement and investment; flood defence funding maintained; tree/peat targets; new National Park; deposit return scheme; limit new incinerators.

- Union and devolution
  - Extend UK Shared Prosperity Fund (3 years), Long‑Term Plan for Towns and Community Ownership Fund UK‑wide; more freeports/investment zones; specific transport/energy projects in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; uphold Windsor Framework and Belfast (Good Friday) Agreement.

- Sex and gender law
  - Legislate that “sex” in Equality Act means biological sex; single legal sex; statutory school guidance on gender‑questioning; protect single‑sex sports/spaces.
